calls.head: The Lightning should tilt the ice
calls.body: The Lightning have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Oilers around the middle. Expect the Lightning to spend more of the night in the Oilers’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

calls.head: Picky vs. trigger-happy
calls.body: On shot quality, Tampa Bay is one of the league’s best, but Edmonton is one of the worst. The more dangerous chances should be the Lightning’s.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Lightning take down the Oilers
paras: John Carlson opened the scoring for the Lightning on the power play midway through the second. Ilya Mikheyev and Nikita Kucherov scored less than four minutes apart midway through the third to push the lead to 3-0. Colton Dach got the Oilers on the board with less than two minutes left.

The Oilers had more of the shots, 24-19, but the Lightning had the better ones. Andrei Vasilevskiy made 23 saves for the Bolts, and Devon Levi stopped 17 of 19 at the other end. The loss ended Levi’s six-game winning streak. By our Swing measure, Erik Černák had the best night of anyone. The Lightning improved to 15-5-2, still first in the Atlantic, while the Oilers dropped to 17-4-3, slipping out of first in the NHL.

items.text: The Oilers’ six-game heater is over.
Nikita Kucherov extended his point streak against Edmonton to seven games.
John Carlson extended his point streak against Edmonton to six games.
